title: A morphism of inverse systems induces a (non-unique) morphism of derived limits
statement: Let $\mathcal D$ be a triangulated category [def-weil-triangulated-category], and let $(K_n,f_n)_{n\geq1}$, $(K'_n,f'_n)_{n\geq1}$ be inverse systems of objects of $\mathcal D$ [def-weil-inverse-system] whose products exist [def-weil-category-product], with transition endomorphisms $1-s$, $1-s'$ [def-weil-tower-transition-endomorphism]. Let $K\xrightarrow{p}\prod_nK_n\xrightarrow{1-s}\prod_nK_n\xrightarrow{\delta}K[1]$ and $K'\xrightarrow{p'}\prod_nK'_n\xrightarrow{1-s'}\prod_nK'_n\xrightarrow{\delta'}K'[1]$ be distinguished triangles (Roos triangles; $K$, $K'$ are derived limits [def-weil-derived-limit]), and let $(\varphi_n):(K_n,f_n)\to(K'_n,f'_n)$ be a morphism of inverse systems. Then there exists a morphism $\varphi:K\to K'$ with $p'\circ\varphi=(\prod_n\varphi_n)\circ p$ and $\varphi[1]\circ\delta=\delta'\circ\prod_n\varphi_n$, i.e. $(\varphi,\prod_n\varphi_n,\prod_n\varphi_n)$ is a morphism of triangles. The morphism $\varphi$ is in general not unique.

We warn the reader that the map $K\to L$ is not unique."
